OP: Mailchimp closed my account (apparently for inactivity) without warning. Support replied that there was nothing they would do and that I should create a new account, leaving me unable to reach customers on my mailing list about a potential security issue. A single automated warning email would have avoided this.

I created an account, verified my email, then sent a test email to that same address. Mailchimp immediately disabled my account's ability to send. My appeal to support was ignored, and the account was eventually deleted and banned.
I got really fed up with MailChimp and their support over this kind of thing and moved to SendX. Haven't looked back.

Mailchimp removed my mailing list and banned my account without notice. Support said it was because I was 'involved in cryptocurrencies' and that all data was wiped. Only after I hinted at public shaming did someone send me a data dump of the emails. I now use Mautic and my own SMTP server.

Friends of mine have had MailChimp accounts deleted or locked without explanation, warning, or recourse, so I wouldn't rely on MC for anything business-critical. Export periodic backups to another provider.

Long-time customer who migrated away: MailChimp has acted as a cash cow and invested very little apart from a recent redesign. Mandrill still isn't integrated years after the two services were combined.
I created an account a couple of years ago and never used it. When I recently tried to log in, the account was deleted and my email banned, even though I'm not tied to any shady business.

One recipient complained about one of our marketing emails, and Mailchimp/Mandrill silently shut off our incoming support-ticket email. We only noticed when a customer called asking why we hadn't replied. A big bag of 'do not recommend'.
They banned me after I migrated a list of 80 newsletter sign-ups from my own website, saying I couldn't confirm how I got the emails. I never went back.

Paid-tier user in 2012: when we moved sending to arpReach + SES and asked to drop back to a free account, Mailchimp said that wasn't allowed. We could keep paying or delete the account. Everything was fine while we used them, but that left a bad taste.
MailChimp removed half the users from a list I hadn't mailed recently, citing unverified sign-ups and spam complaints, even though all the sign-ups came through MailChimp's own forms.
As a regular email recipient, I appreciate Mailchimp's heavy hand with lists it deems bad. It keeps a high standard for list and email quality, and the shutdown stories often involve spammy content.
Workaround: I just exported my Mailchimp subscriber list for safekeeping, and would like to automate that as a monthly job.

Opening the browser inspector and reloading Mailchimp shows 'Request Blocked... the IP address you're using looks suspicious.' Another user said it happened to them and they could reproduce it from different network locations.

As a developer I often have devtools open. When I help marketing with a Mailchimp automation in the same tab, I get banned for the day. That explains why Mailchimp has been failing to load for me lately.

In the drag-and-drop builder I added a Code module with a style tag. Because it rendered no space, the module became unclickable in the UI. I injected br tags via the Inspector to reach it and got IP-blocked.

Mailchimp's text editor failed to load on International Women's Day, so we couldn't send our promotion. I showed the library error in the web inspector plus a screencast, wasn't blocked, and got a refund.

Blocking devtools is anticompetitive: if you need to switch senders, the inspector is the only clean way to get an email's HTML into another ESP. One user said they'd plan to switch ASAP if their agency were hit by this.
Workarounds suggested for the devtools block: open devtools in a separate, undocked window before loading the page, or disable breakpoints in Firefox so debugger-timing checks fail.
I wondered why I kept getting blocked from Mailchimp. I accidentally open dev tools all the time.
